former_name: Spirax-Sarco Engineering plc (renamed to Spirax Group plc following shareholder approval at the May 2024 AGM, effective 3 June 2024)
sector: Industrials - Thermal Energy and Fluid Technology
overview: Spirax Group is a UK-headquartered (Cheltenham) global engineering group providing critical thermal energy management and fluid technology solutions used in industrial processes such as cleaning, sterilising, cooking, heating, and biopharmaceutical manufacturing. The Group operates through three Businesses -- Steam Thermal Solutions (STS), Electric Thermal Solutions (ETS), and Watson-Marlow Fluid Technology Solutions (WMFTS, the peristaltic pump business) -- serving over 100,000 customers across nearly 70 countries via a large direct sales and service engineer force (~2,900 engineers). The Group has been listed on the LSE since 1959 (ticker SPX, FTSE 100 constituent) and renamed itself from Spirax-Sarco Engineering plc to Spirax Group plc in June 2024 to better distinguish the parent Group from its Spirax Sarco trading division within STS.

business_model.summary: Spirax Group earns revenue by designing, manufacturing, and directly selling (via its own engineers, not mainly distributors) specialised equipment and engineered solutions for steam systems, electric process heating, and peristaltic pumping/fluid transfer. The business model is distinguished by a high proportion of recurring, non-discretionary revenue: approximately 85% of sales come from maintenance/repair (MRO, ~45% of sales) and smaller 'solution-sales' (~40% of sales combined with MRO) funded from customers' local operating budgets rather than capital expenditure budgets, with only ~15% of sales tied to large, lumpier capital projects that are more cyclical. No single customer accounts for more than ~1% of Group sales, and ~60% of sales are to defensive, less-cyclical end sectors (Food & Beverage, Pharma/Biotech, Healthcare, Water & Wastewater).

revenue_streams.name: Steam Thermal Solutions (STS)
revenue_streams.description: Design and supply of industrial/commercial steam systems, condensate management, controls and thermal energy management (incl. Spirax Sarco and Gestra brands); FY2025 revenue £853.4m (down 2% reported, +1% organic), weighed down by weak large-project demand in China/Korea; H1 2026 organic growth +1%

revenue_streams.name: Electric Thermal Solutions (ETS)
revenue_streams.description: Electrification solutions for industrial process heating (Process Heating, Equipment Heating, and now-separate Heat Trace division), including Chromalox, Thermocoax and Vulcanic brands; serves Semiconductor, Datacentre, Oil & Gas, Nuclear, and Aerospace & Defence customers; FY2025 revenue £441.3m (+9% reported, +11% organic); H1 2026 organic growth +11%, the strongest of the three divisions

revenue_streams.name: Watson-Marlow Fluid Technology Solutions (WMFTS)
revenue_streams.description: World-leading peristaltic pump and fluid-path technology business serving Biopharm (monoclonal antibodies, recombinant DNA, cell & gene therapies) and Process Industries (Mining, Wastewater); FY2025 revenue £408.2m (+4% reported, +6% organic); H1 2026 organic growth +7%, with Biopharm orders at highest level since the 2021 COVID peak

business_model.customer_type: B2B industrial/commercial end-customers (Food & Beverage, Pharma/Biotech, Oil & Gas, Semiconductor, Datacentres, Healthcare, Mining, Wastewater, OEM Machinery) across enterprise and mid-market accounts, served directly rather than primarily through distributors, though STS USA increasingly co-generates demand with ~22 distribution partners
business_model.geographic_mix: EMEA 44% of sales, Americas 38%, APAC 18% (per 2025/2026 investor presentation); ~70 countries with direct sales presence; China and Korea are more exposed to large-project/capital-expenditure cyclicality than other regions
business_model.unit_economics: Typical invoice values range from ~£1.5k (maintenance/repair), to £10k-£80k (solution-sales), to >£100k (large projects); ~85% of revenue is funded from customers' local operating budgets (non-discretionary, recurring-like), with only ~15% tied to capital-budget-funded large projects; Group targets mid-single-digit organic revenue growth at roughly 2x global Industrial Production (IP) growth, high-margin operations (20%+ Group adjusted operating margin), and ROCE of 36% (2025) with a medium-term ambition for ROIC to progress above 15% (2025 ROIC: 13.1%)

main_competitors: Armstrong International (steam, privately-held, strong in Oil & Gas)
Ingersoll Rand (entered peristaltic pump/bioprocessing adjacency via a ~$2.3bn acquisition reported as a direct challenge to Watson-Marlow's niche)
Honeywell, Emerson, Danfoss (broader industrial heating/process control)
General Electric, ITT, Parker Hannifin (diversified industrial automation/fluid control peers)
competitive_position.market_position: Global leader in industrial steam systems (STS/Spirax Sarco) and in peristaltic pumps (WMFTS/Watson-Marlow Bredel, described by the company and third parties as world market leader), with ETS holding niche leadership positions in process/equipment heating and heat tracing built through bolt-on acquisitions (Chromalox, Thermocoax, Vulcanic, Durex). Most direct steam and electric-heating competitors are privately held, making market-share comparisons difficult, but Spirax is consistently cited as the largest listed pure-play in thermal energy management.

moat_factors.description: ~2,900 direct sales and service engineers who 'walk the plant' build deep, sticky technical relationships with customers that are difficult for distributors or lower-touch competitors to replicate; drives high-margin MRO and solution-sales (85% of revenue) funded from recurring local operating budgets

Over 100,000 customers and a large global installed base of steam, electric heating, and pump equipment generate durable, high-margin aftermarket (MRO) revenue; digital connectivity initiatives (e.g., STS's growing base of connected sites/assets) are extending this advantage into predictive/condition-based service

moat_factors.factor: Engineering/technical expertise and applied design capability
moat_factors.description: Proprietary technologies (e.g., PoweringZero and TargetZero decarbonisation solutions, SteamVolt, Electrofit, Bredel pump technology) and deep applications engineering allow Spirax to solve complex, customer-specific thermal/fluid problems that generic suppliers cannot

Over 30 regional manufacturing plants positioned close to sales operating companies reduce lead times, build supply chain agility, and partially mitigate tariff/trade exposure (e.g., US manufacturing for Chromalox/Devens reduces tariff impact)

moat_factors.strength: strong in WMFTS, developing in ETS
moat_factors.description: Watson-Marlow's peristaltic pump technology has few direct scaled public competitors and strong share in Biopharm bioprocessing; ETS's proprietary electrification technology (Medium/Low Voltage heaters) is newer and still scaling toward its 20% margin target

No customer >1% of sales and exposure to multiple defensive end-markets (Food & Beverage, Healthcare, Pharma) reduces cyclicality versus pure capital-goods peers, though STS remains exposed to China/Korea large-project cyclicality

weaknesses: STS China/Korea large-project exposure remains a drag; large projects are tied to customer capital-expenditure cycles that are currently subdued amid tariff/trade uncertainty

ETS margin (17.2% H1 2026) still well below the Group's other divisions and its own 20% medium-term target, reflecting a newer, less mature business built through acquisition integration (Chromalox, Thermocoax, Vulcanic) plus ramp-up costs for the new Ogden, Utah Medium Voltage facility

Emerging competitive threat to Watson-Marlow's peristaltic pump/bioprocessing niche from larger, better-capitalised entrants (e.g., Ingersoll Rand's reported $2.3bn move into integrated pump/tubing solutions)
Most core steam and electric-heating competitors are privately held, making competitive benchmarking and market-share tracking difficult for investors
Currency exposure is structurally adverse to reported (GBP) results given sterling strength versus EUR/USD/RMB/KRW, muting reported growth even when organic growth is healthy

Group adjusted operating margin (20.0% FY2025) declined slightly on a reported basis in 2024-2025 and the business is mid-way through a multi-year reinvestment and restructuring program, creating near-term margin and cash-conversion volatility (H1 2026 adjusted cash conversion fell to 54% from 61% due to planned inventory build and higher ETS receivables)

growth_drivers: Together for Growth Strategy (launched at October 2024 Capital Markets Day): five Growth Drivers -- Commercial Excellence, Operational Excellence, Organisational Fitness, Digital and Services, and Decarbonising Thermal Energy -- targeting mid-single-digit organic growth at ~2x global IP, margin progression, and ROIC improving to >15%

Decarbonisation of thermal energy (PoweringZero and TargetZero offerings): adds an estimated ~£7bn (combined ~£5bn PoweringZero + ~£2bn TargetZero) to the Group's ~£18bn current addressable market, driven by electrification of steam generation and broader industrial decarbonisation beyond steam

Secular structural tailwinds: emerging middle class (800m+ entering middle class, driving capacity expansion), ageing global population (Biopharm demand, 17% of Group sales in 2025), resource efficiency/sustainability mandates, and growth in high-growth target sectors (Semiconductor, Datacentres, EV Batteries, Nuclear, Aerospace & Defence, Mining, Wastewater)

Datacentre/AI infrastructure exposure: ETS liquid-cooled load bank temperature management for datacentre OEM customers is a newly identified, fast-growing opportunity, with STS (air eliminators) and WMFTS (liquid-cooling hoses) also positioned to benefit

Biopharm demand recovery in WMFTS: new order intake running ahead of sales, with Q2 2026 orders at the highest quarterly level since the 2021 COVID-era peak, driven by monoclonal antibodies, recombinant DNA, and cell & gene therapy growth

Digital and Services expansion: growing base of connected STS sites (over 2,350 by mid-2026, up from 2,000 at end-2025) and WMFTS machine-learning-enabled Bredel pump pilots, generating pull-through MRO/service revenue; early build-out of agentic AI tools for sales quoting and design

Restructuring-driven annualised cost savings of ~£40 million (completed 2025), being substantially reinvested into sales headcount, digital tools, new product development, and decarbonisation capability to fund future compounding growth

Disciplined bolt-on M&A in ETS (historical acquisitions of Chromalox, Thermocoax, Vulcanic, Durex) continues to be part of the capital allocation framework (after organic investment and the progressive dividend) for further electrification/niche-technology expansion

Capital allocation framework supporting both growth and shareholder returns: organic investment first (at 36% ROCE), then progressive dividend (58-year track record, 2.0x-2.5x cover target), then disciplined bolt-on M&A, then additional returns of surplus capital

business.description: Rated by the company itself as having 'very high' risk velocity and the Group accepts a 'high' risk appetite here; global operations in historically volatile regions create exposure to demand volatility, credit/liquidity risk, and currency risk; China and Korea large-project weakness in 2025/H1 2026 is a live example

business.risk: Inability to identify or respond to changing customer needs (digital/non-digital)
business.description: Principal Risk acknowledged by the Board; failure to keep pace with digital transformation or evolving customer requirements (including decarbonisation demands) could erode demand over time; mitigated via competitor analysis and the Digital and Services Growth Driver
Group's bolt-on M&A strategy (Chromalox, Thermocoax, Vulcanic, Durex) carries integration risk; poor integration could cause underperformance, poor talent retention, or failure to meet customer needs

business.risk: Loss of manufacturing output at a Group factory
business.description: Natural disasters, industrial action, or accidents at any of 30+ manufacturing plants could disrupt customer service; mitigated by geographic spread, multiple supply sources, and insurance

Larger, better-capitalised entrants (e.g., Ingersoll Rand's reported move into integrated peristaltic pump/tubing solutions) could erode WMFTS's historically strong competitive position in bioprocessing

business.risk: STS large-project cyclicality concentrated in China/Korea
business.description: China and Korea accounted for 22% of STS sales in 2024; capital-expenditure deferrals (observed in 2025 amid Korean political instability and Chinese demand weakness) directly hit large-project STS revenue and margin phasing

financial.description: Reported in GBP but with large EUR, USD, RMB and KRW exposures; sterling strength in 2025 created a 3% adverse currency impact on sales and 4% on adjusted operating profit; net transactional exposure ~£150m annually from UK-manufactured exports versus EUR/USD-priced imports

Net debt/EBITDA of 1.5x-1.6x (within the 1.0x-1.5x target range, periodically exceeded for M&A), interest cover of 12x; debt covenants include a 3.5x leverage covenant and 3.0x interest cover covenant with material headroom; successfully refinanced a maturing EUR120m US Private Placement in H1 2026

H1 2026 adjusted cash conversion fell to 54% (from 61% in H1 2025) due to a planned inventory build (mitigating Middle East conflict-related supply chain disruption risk) and higher ETS receivables from strong sales growth; full-year cash conversion guided to be similar to 2025 levels (89%)
Ongoing employer contributions to defined benefit pension schemes; not flagged as a major concern in recent filings

regulatory.risk: Breach of legal and regulatory requirements (including Anti-Bribery and Corruption laws)
regulatory.description: Principal Risk given the Group's growing footprint in new, increasingly complex legislative jurisdictions; breaches could trigger fines, loss of business and reputational damage; mitigated through biennial ABC training, whistleblowing hotline (Safecall), and ongoing monitoring of commercial agreements

Evolving, uncertain tariff regimes (explicitly cited as an ongoing area of Board focus) affect customer capital investment confidence and costs; mitigated via US local manufacturing presence, pricing/surcharge actions and limited reorganisation of manufacturing activity

regulatory.risk: Evolving UK/EU sustainability and climate disclosure requirements
regulatory.description: UK Climate-related Financial Disclosure (CFD) regulations and TCFD-aligned reporting create ongoing compliance obligations; Group reports full alignment currently

macro.description: Global IP growth of 2.1% in 2025 (1.7% excluding China) and only 1.8%-1.9% expected in 2026 remains well below historical norms; IP is a key demand driver, particularly for STS large projects; key markets representing ~50% of Group revenue (Germany, USA, France, Italy, UK) all showing subdued IP

macro.risk: Geopolitical conflict disruption to supply chains
macro.description: H1 2026 saw a deliberate inventory build specifically to mitigate anticipated supply chain disruption from the conflict in the Middle East, denting near-term cash conversion

Net financing expense (~£38m guided for 2026) is sensitive to floating-rate debt costs and average net debt levels, though the Group has been actively reducing average debt and benefiting from cash centralisation

Explicitly upgraded risk appetite rating from Very Low to Low in 2025 due to rising high-profile cyber incidents industry-wide and increasingly sophisticated AI-enabled attacks; Principal Risk with ongoing NIST-framework assessment and incident response investment

macro_factors.industry_outlook: Global Industrial Production (IP) growth was 2.1% in 2025 (1.7% excluding China) and is forecast at only 1.8%-1.9% for 2026, with particular weakness in the US, Germany, France, Italy and UK -- markets representing roughly half of Group revenue. Despite subdued IP, Spirax has consistently delivered organic growth at ~2x-2.5x IP via its direct-sales, MRO-weighted model, and management continues to see substantial medium/long-term structural growth from decarbonisation, Biopharm, Semiconductor and Datacentre end-markets.
macro_factors.cyclicality: Moderate -- roughly 85% of revenue (MRO + solution-sales) is funded from customers' recurring local operating budgets and relatively resilient through cycles; the remaining ~15% (large capital projects, concentrated in STS China/Korea) is meaningfully more cyclical and capital-expenditure-cycle dependent.
macro_factors.interest_rate_sensitivity: Low-moderate -- net debt/EBITDA of ~1.5x-1.6x with moderate floating-rate exposure; net financing expense guided at ~£38m for 2026, not a dominant driver of earnings.
macro_factors.currency_exposure: High -- GBP reporting currency against large EUR, USD, Chinese renminbi and Korean won exposures; sterling strength has been a persistent headwind to reported (though not organic) growth in 2024-2025; UK-manufactured, sterling-invoiced exports versus EUR/USD-priced imports create ~£150m of net transactional FX exposure.
macro_factors.regulatory_environment: Operates under increasingly complex multi-jurisdictional legal/regulatory frameworks as the Group expands into new territories; Anti-Bribery and Corruption compliance, UK Corporate Governance Code (Provision 29 effective 2026), and UK Climate-related Financial Disclosure/TCFD requirements are the most material current compliance threads; no material pending litigation or regulatory enforcement action disclosed in filings reviewed.

recent_developments.event: H1 2026 results: revenue £863.8m (+5% reported and organic), statutory operating profit £154.2m (+44%, aided by absence of prior-year one-off restructuring charges), adjusted operating profit £171.1m (+8% reported, +6% organic), adjusted operating margin 19.8% (+10bps organic), adjusted EPS 150.0p (+9%), interim dividend 50.4p (+3%). All three divisions grew organically (STS +1%, ETS +11%, WMFTS +7%). Company reiterated full-year guidance of mid-single-digit organic revenue growth and organic margin progression above the 2025 margin of 20.0%. Net debt £618.2m, leverage 1.6x (within target range).

Successfully refinanced a maturing EUR120m US Private Placement with EUR80m of new US Private Placement notes (EUR50m 4-year notes to 2030, EUR30m 5-year notes to 2031) and increased/extended an existing EUR90m Bank Term Loan to EUR110m, maturing 2029.

AGM held; Board confirmed continuing confidence in delivering FY2025 Capital Markets Day medium-term targets, and 'above these targets in the longer term'; new Audit and Risk Committee established effective 1 April 2026 (combining prior separate Audit Committee function).

FY2025 full-year results: revenue £1,702.9m (+2% reported, +5% organic), adjusted operating profit £339.9m (+2% reported, +6% organic), adjusted operating margin 20.0% (30bps higher organically, 10bps lower reported due to FX), adjusted EPS 296.3p (+3%), statutory operating profit £265.4m (-13%, reflecting a £39.9m restructuring charge), full-year dividend 170.0p (+3%, 58th consecutive year of dividend increases). ROCE 36.0%, ROIC 13.1%. Completed the ~£40m annualised cost-saving restructuring programme (STS EMEA reorganisation, WMFTS EMEA sectorisation, Heat Trace established as a separate ETS division).

Organisational restructuring: STS EMEA simplified management structure and sectorised sales teams; WMFTS EMEA moved from geographic to sectorised sales focus; Heat Trace split out from Process Heating into its own ETS division with dedicated sales engineers; ETS completed its new Medium Voltage manufacturing facility in Ogden, Utah, supporting growth capacity.

Board changes: Jane Kingston stepped down from the Board (September 2025); Maria Antoniou joined the Board (June 2025) as Chair of the Remuneration Committee; Andrew Kemp joined the Board (November 2025) ahead of succeeding Kevin Thompson as Audit Committee Chair in April 2026; Kevin Thompson to step down at the 2026 AGM after seven years.

recent_developments.event: Tim Cobbold completed his first full year as Group Chair, supporting CEO Nimesh Patel's implementation of the Together for Growth Strategy launched at the October 2024 Capital Markets Day.

Company legal name changed from Spirax-Sarco Engineering plc to Spirax Group plc, following shareholder approval at the May 2024 AGM, to better distinguish the parent Group from its Spirax Sarco trading division (part of STS); ticker (SPX) and financial reporting unaffected.

Capital Markets Day held in London; management set out the Together for Growth Strategy and associated medium-term targets (mid-single-digit organic sales growth at ~2x global IP, margin progression toward divisional targets of ~23.5% STS / ~20% ETS / >30% WMFTS, cash conversion >80%, ROIC improving to >15%, leverage maintained at 1.0x-1.5x net debt/EBITDA).

guidance.management_commentary: CEO Nimesh Patel described H1 2026 as 'resilient mid-single-digit organic growth in revenue and profit, well ahead of IP,' noting that 'driving growth ahead of our markets, in spite of external conditions, is now becoming embedded in how we operate.' He cited 'continuing momentum in end markets such as Semicon and Biopharm as well as strong orderbooks' underpinning expectations for H2 growth, and reiterated that the Together for Growth Strategy is 'strengthening the Group's differentiated business model, competitive leadership and resilience,' with the Group 'on track to deliver the medium-term targets... set out... in October 2024; and above these targets in the longer term.' CFO Louisa Burdett's review emphasized that STS margin softness in H1 reflects shipment phasing and first-half-weighted growth investment rather than structural deterioration, with full-year STS margin expected broadly in line with 2025.

bull_case: Resilient, high-quality revenue mix: ~85% of sales are MRO/solution-sales funded from customers' recurring local operating budgets rather than discretionary capital budgets, supporting durable mid-single-digit organic growth at ~2x global IP even through a weak macro backdrop

Three complementary, structurally advantaged franchises (global steam leadership in STS, fast-growing niche electrification leadership in ETS, and world-leading peristaltic pump technology in WMFTS) provide diversified, multi-decade growth optionality, especially from decarbonisation (combined ~£7bn addressable market expansion via PoweringZero/TargetZero), Biopharm recovery, and Semiconductor/Datacentre electrification demand

Exceptional, long-track-record capital efficiency and shareholder returns: ROCE of 36% (2025), a 58-consecutive-year dividend growth record, and a disciplined capital allocation hierarchy (organic investment first, then dividends, then bolt-on M&A, then additional returns) under-pin a durable compounding growth and total-shareholder-return thesis

Completed restructuring (£40m annualised savings) is being reinvested into Digital and Services and decarbonisation capability, positioning the Group to capture a larger share of its expanding addressable market while maintaining margin discipline and improving ROIC toward a >15% medium-term target

ETS margin expansion runway: four of five identified margin levers (legacy order clearance, operating leverage, manufacturing efficiencies, favourable Semicon/Heat Trace mix) are already delivering, with a clear path toward the ~20% medium-term ETS margin target as the newest, least mature of the three Businesses matures
bear_case: Persistently weak global Industrial Production growth (just 1.8-1.9% forecast for 2026, with the UK/Germany/France/Italy/USA -- ~50% of Group revenue -- all subdued) continues to suppress large-project demand, particularly in STS China/Korea, and could compress overall growth below the mid-single-digit target if conditions deteriorate further

Emerging, better-capitalised competitive threats to Watson-Marlow's historically dominant peristaltic pump niche (e.g., reported $2.3bn Ingersoll Rand move into integrated pump/tubing solutions) could erode WMFTS's premium margins and market position over time

ETS remains the Group's least mature, lowest-margin division (17.2% H1 2026 vs. ~20% target, and well below STS's 22% and WMFTS's 27.5%), built substantially through acquisition integration, and still faces ramp-up costs (e.g., the new Ogden, Utah facility) that could delay margin delivery if execution falters

Significant GBP currency headwind risk given large EUR/USD/RMB/KRW exposures; a further strengthening of sterling (as seen in 2024-2025) mutes reported growth and profit even when underlying organic performance is healthy, potentially disappointing investors focused on headline (not organic) numbers

Elevated and rising cybersecurity risk (explicitly upgraded by the Board from Very Low to Low risk appetite in 2025) and ongoing exposure to trade tariff/protectionism uncertainty add cost and operational risk to a business with 30+ global manufacturing sites and complex cross-border supply chains

Near-term cash conversion volatility (54% in H1 2026 vs. 61% in H1 2025, driven by planned inventory builds and rising ETS receivables) illustrates working-capital sensitivity to strong growth phases, which could pressure free cash flow if sales growth outpaces collections/inventory discipline
